literal: The emperor heard the empress dowager was improper, but did not yet believe it.
idiomatic: The emperor had heard the empress dowager was behaving improperly, but did not yet believe it.

literal: Later when he attended the empress dowager, he saw two young nuns, took pleasure in them and summoned them — they were men.
idiomatic: Later, when he went to attend the empress dowager, he saw two young nuns, took a liking to them, and summoned them — only to find they were men in disguise.

literal: Thereupon the Tanxian affair also broke; all were executed by law.
idiomatic: Thereupon the affair with the monk Tanxian also came to light; all involved were executed.

literal: Together they also killed the three commandery ladies of Prince of Yuanshan, all whom the empress dowager had been intimate with.
idiomatic: They also executed the three commandery ladies of the Prince of Yuanshan, all favorites of the empress dowager.

literal: The emperor from Jinyang escorted the empress dowager back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly met a great wind.
idiomatic: The emperor escorted the empress dowager back from Jinyang to Ye; at Zimo they were suddenly struck by a violent wind.

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Wei Sengqia understood wind angles.
idiomatic: The attendant-in-ordinary Wei Sengqia was skilled in reading omens from the wind.

literal: He memorialized saying: "At this moment there will be violent treason.
idiomatic: He reported, "At this very moment there will be violent treason.

literal: " The emperor falsely said there was an emergency in Ye, bent his bow and wound the string, and galloped into the Southern City.
idiomatic: " The emperor pretended there was an emergency in Ye, strung his bow, and galloped into the Southern City.

literal: He ordered Deng Changyan to imprison the empress dowager in the Northern Palace.
idiomatic: He ordered Deng Changyan to confine the empress dowager in the Northern Palace.

literal: There was still an edict: inside and outside, all kin were forbidden to see the empress dowager.
idiomatic: An edict followed forbidding all relatives, inside and outside the palace, from seeing the empress dowager.

literal: After a long time the emperor welcomed the empress dowager back.
idiomatic: After a long while the emperor brought the empress dowager back.

literal: When the empress dowager first heard envoys had come, she was greatly alarmed, fearing the unforeseen.
idiomatic: When the empress dowager first heard that envoys had arrived, she was terrified, fearing the worst.

literal: Whenever the empress dowager set out food, the emperor also did not dare taste it.
idiomatic: Whenever the empress dowager prepared food, the emperor would not dare to taste it.

literal: A Zhou envoy Yuan Wei came on a mission of courtesy and composed the Narrative of a Journey, recounting Duke Zhuang of Zheng's overcoming of Duan and removal of Lady Jiang.
idiomatic: A Zhou envoy, Yuan Wei, came on a diplomatic visit and composed the Narrative of a Journey, recounting how Duke Zhuang of Zheng overcame his brother Duan and banished their mother Lady Jiang.

literal: Though the writing was not skilled, at the time they were deeply ashamed.
idiomatic: Though the piece was not well written, at the time it caused deep shame.

literal: When Qi perished he entered Zhou and indulged in lewd wickedness without restraint.
idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell he entered Northern Zhou and gave himself over to lewd and wicked conduct.

literal: In the Kaihuang era he died.
idiomatic: He died during the Kaihuang reign.

literal: Lady of Manifest Virtue Li was the daughter of Li Shurang of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: The Lady of Manifest Virtue, surnamed Li, was the daughter of Li Shurang of Zhao commandery.

literal: At first she was a consort of Emperor Jing of Wei; Wucheng took her in.
idiomatic: She had first been a consort of Emperor Jing of Wei; Wucheng took her into the palace.

literal: She bore Prince of Nanyang Rensheng and became grand consort.
idiomatic: She bore the Prince of Nanyang, Rensheng, and was made grand consort.

literal: Her elder sister was consort to Prince of Nan'an Si; for her husband's rebellion she was burned to death.
idiomatic: Her elder sister had been consort to the Prince of Nan'an, Si; when he rebelled she was burned alive.

literal: The grand consort heard of it, went mad, and died.
idiomatic: When the grand consort heard of it she went mad and died.

literal: Wenzuan's consort and the younger sister of the inner attendant Lu Lecha — Wucheng took both as consorts.
idiomatic: Wenzuan's consort and the younger sister of the inner attendant Lu Lecha — Wucheng took both as his consorts.

literal: After Wucheng's death the Hu empress ordered the two consorts to kill themselves.
idiomatic: After Wucheng died, Empress Hu ordered the two consorts to take their own lives.

literal: The two consorts wept in grief; the later lord was moved to compassion for them.
idiomatic: The two consorts wept bitterly; the later lord was moved to pity.

literal: Privately he sent them clothing and had them go outside to avoid it.
idiomatic: He secretly sent them clothing and let them leave the palace to escape.

literal: Lu raised the Prince of Huainan and later became grand consort.
idiomatic: Lu raised the Prince of Huainan and later became grand consort.

literal: There was also Consort Ma, who also won favor; the empress was jealous and she hanged herself.
idiomatic: There was also Consort Ma, who likewise won favor; the empress, jealous, drove her to hang herself.

literal: Peng Rong and Ren Xiang both had daughters; because of their fathers' and brothers' cases they all entered the palace and were favored by Wenzuan.
idiomatic: Peng Rong and Ren Xiang each had daughters who, implicated in their fathers' and brothers' crimes, were sent into the palace and favored by Wenzuan.

literal: Wucheng made Peng a lady and raised Prince of Qi'an; Ren bore Prince of Danyang — both became grand consorts.
idiomatic: Wucheng made Peng a lady and had her raise the Prince of Qi'an; Ren bore the Prince of Danyang — both were made grand consorts.

literal: The later lord's empress Hulu was the daughter of Left Chancellor Guang.
idiomatic: The later lord's empress, surnamed Hulu, was the daughter of the Left Chancellor Guang.

literal: At first she was the crown prince's consort; when the later lord received the abdication she was established empress.
idiomatic: She had first been crown princess; when the later lord succeeded to the throne she was made empress.

literal: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she bore a daughter.
idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she gave birth to a daughter.

literal: The emperor wished to please Guang and falsely claimed a son had been born; for this he proclaimed a great amnesty.
idiomatic: The emperor wished to please Guang and falsely announced that a son had been born; a great amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: When Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace; later she was ordered to become a nun.
idiomatic: After Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace and later ordered to become a nun.

literal: When Qi perished she was married as wife to Yuan Ren, opening the government.
idiomatic: When Qi fell she was married to Yuan Ren, a commander of the opening-the-government rank.

literal: The later lord's empress Hu was the daughter of Prince of Longdong Changren.
idiomatic: The later lord's empress, surnamed Hu, was the daughter of the Prince of Longdong, Changren.

literal: Empress Dowager Hu had lost the way of a mother's propriety and was deeply ashamed; she wished to please the later lord, so she adorned the empress within the palace.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu, having failed in maternal propriety, was deeply ashamed and wished to please the later lord, so she had the empress dressed and adorned within the palace.

literal: She had the emperor see her.
idiomatic: She arranged for the emperor to see her.

literal: The emperor was indeed pleased; she was established Lady of Manifest Virtue, advanced to Left Zhaoyi, and greatly favored.
idiomatic: The emperor was indeed pleased; she was made Lady of Manifest Virtue, promoted to Left Zhaoyi, and greatly favored.

literal: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lady Lu wished to replace her with Lady Mu; the empress dowager did not permit it.
idiomatic: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lady Lu wanted Lady Mu to replace her; the empress dowager refused.

literal: Zu Xiaozheng requested establishing Hu Zhaoyi; she then ascended as empress.
idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng urged that Hu Zhaoyi be made empress, and she was duly elevated.

literal: Lady Lu had not urged the establishment and also had her heart set on Lady Mu; afterward before the empress dowager she made a face and said: "What kind of close niece is this, to speak such words!
idiomatic: Lady Lu had not supported the elevation and still favored Lady Mu; later, before the empress dowager, she scowled and said, "What sort of close niece is this, to speak such words!

literal: " The empress dowager asked what words.
idiomatic: " The empress dowager asked what she had said.

literal: She said: "Cannot be spoken.
idiomatic: She replied, "It cannot be repeated.

literal: " Pressed repeatedly, she then said: "She told everyone that the empress dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot be taken as instruction.
idiomatic: " Pressed again and again, she finally said, "She told everyone that the empress dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot serve as a model.

literal: " The empress dowager was greatly angered, summoned the empress out, had her head shaved, and sent her back home.
idiomatic: " The empress dowager flew into a rage, had the empress brought out, shaved her head, and sent her home.

literal: The emperor missed her and often sent poems to convey his feelings.
idiomatic: The emperor longed for her and often sent poems to express his feelings.

literal: Later she and the deposed Empress Hulu were both summoned within.
idiomatic: Later she and the deposed Empress Hulu were both summoned back into the palace.

literal: Within days Ye was not held; the empress also remarried, it is said.
idiomatic: Within days Ye fell; the empress is said to have remarried as well.

literal: The later lord's empress Mu, named Xieli, was originally a attendant maid of Empress Hulu.
idiomatic: The later lord's empress Mu, named Xieli, had originally been a attendant maid of Empress Hulu.

literal: Her mother was named Qingxiao, originally a maid of Muzilun; she passed into the household of Attendant-in-ordinary Song Qindao, and through illicit relations bore the empress — her clan was unknown; some say the empress was Song Qindao's own daughter.
idiomatic: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid of Muzilun, then entered the household of the attendant-in-ordinary Song Qindao; an illicit affair produced the future empress, whose lineage was unknown — some said she was Song Qindao's own daughter.

literal: Her childhood name was Yellow Flower; her later name was Sheli.
idiomatic: Her childhood name was Yellow Flower; her formal name was Sheli.

literal: Song Qindao's wife was jealous; Qingxiao's face was tattooed with the character Song.
idiomatic: Song Qindao's wife was jealous; Qingxiao's face was branded with the character for Song.

literal: When Song Qindao was executed, Yellow Flower for this reason entered the palace.
idiomatic: When Song Qindao was executed, Yellow Flower entered the palace for that reason.

literal: She won favor from the later lord; within the palace she was called "Grand Supervisor Sheli."
idiomatic: She won the later lord's favor; within the palace she was called "Grand Supervisor Sheli."

literal: Female attendant-in-ordinary Lady Lu the Great Matriarch knew of her favor and raised her as a daughter, recommending her as Lady of Manifest Virtue.
idiomatic: The female attendant-in-ordinary Lady Lu the Great Matriarch, knowing of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Manifest Virtue.

literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she bore the prince Heng.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she bore the prince Heng.

literal: At that time the later lord had no heir; Lu secretly cultivated favor, saying the task of nurturing by a subject could not be without a master.
idiomatic: At that time the later lord had no heir; Lu cultivated favor in secret, arguing that the duty of raising the child by a subject required a recognized master.

literal: Then Empress Hulu, the chancellor Guang's daughter, feared her resentment and first had the mother raise him and establish him crown prince.
idiomatic: Empress Hulu, daughter of Chancellor Guang, fearing resentment, first had the mother raise the child and had him named crown prince.

literal: Lu, because the state's surname was weighty and Mu and Lu faced each other, also memorialized granting the surname Mu.
idiomatic: Lu, because the imperial surname carried great weight and the names Mu and Lu paired well, also petitioned that the surname Mu be granted.

literal: When the Hu commoner was deposed, Lu had helped.
idiomatic: When the Hu consort was deposed, Lu had assisted.

literal: Therefore she was then established empress; a great amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: Therefore she was established empress and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: Earlier, Quelling-Insurgency General Yuan Zhenglie in the eastern waters of Ye city obtained a seal and presented it; the inscription read "Heavenly Empress Seal" — probably made by the Shi clan.
idiomatic: Earlier, Quelling-Insurgency General Yuan Zhenglie had found a seal in the eastern waters of Ye and presented it; the inscription read "Heavenly Empress Seal," probably a relic of the Shi clan.

literal: An edict was issued to announce it, taking it as an omen for Empress Mu.
idiomatic: An edict proclaimed it far and wide, treating it as a portent for Empress Mu.

literal: Wucheng for Empress Hu made pearl skirt-trousers; the cost was beyond reckoning; they were burned in a fire.
idiomatic: Wucheng had pearl skirt-trousers made for Empress Hu at incalculable cost; they were destroyed in a fire.

literal: After the later lord established Empress Mu, he again had them made for her.
idiomatic: After the later lord made Empress Mu, he had them made again for her.

literal: It happened that Emperor Wu of Zhou suffered the empress dowager's mourning; he ordered Attendant-in-ordinary Xue Gu, Kang Mai, and others as condolence envoys, and also sent merchant Hu with thirty thousand bolts of brocade and silk together with the condolence envoys.
idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for his empress dowager; he sent the attendant-in-ordinary Xue Gu, Kang Mai, and others as condolence envoys, and also dispatched a merchant Hu with thirty thousand bolts of brocade and silk to accompany them.

literal: They wished to buy pearls to make a seven-jewel carriage for the empress.
idiomatic: They intended to buy pearls to build a seven-jewel carriage for the empress.

literal: The Zhou people would not trade; yet in the end it was made.
idiomatic: The Zhou would not sell; nevertheless the carriage was built in the end.

literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said: "Yellow Flower's force is about to fall; clear goblets fill the cup and pour.
idiomatic: Earlier a children's rhyme had run, "Yellow Flower's force is about to fall; clear goblets fill to the brim and pour.

literal: " It spoke of Yellow Flower not lasting long.
idiomatic: " It meant that Yellow Flower would not last long.

literal: After the later lord himself established Empress Mu, he drank in stupor without limit; hence "clear goblets fill the cup and pour."
idiomatic: After the later lord himself established Empress Mu, he drank without measure in a stupor — hence "clear goblets fill to the brim and pour."

literal: Lu ended Luotipo and ordered the surname changed to Mu;
idiomatic: Lu dismissed Luotipo and ordered his surname changed to Mu;

literal: Lu, the Great Matriarch.
idiomatic: Lu was styled the Great Matriarch.

literal: All because of the empress.
idiomatic: All of this was for the empress's sake.

literal: Afterward she took Lu as mother and Luotipo as family and no longer attended to Qingxiao.
idiomatic: Afterward she took Lu as her mother and Luotipo as her family, and no longer paid heed to Qingxiao.

literal: Qingxiao later treated her own face to seek a meeting; Lady Lu the Great Matriarch had her imprisoned and guarded and in the end she could not be seen.
idiomatic: Qingxiao later tried to heal her face and beg for an audience; Lady Lu the Great Matriarch had her confined under guard, and she was never allowed to see her daughter.

literal: Consort Feng Shufei, named Xiaolian, was originally a attendant maid of the Great Empress Mu.
idiomatic: Consort Feng Shufei, named Xiaolian, had originally been a attendant maid of the Great Empress Mu.

literal: When the Great Empress Mu's love waned, on the fifth day of the fifth month she was presented — she was called "Extending Life."
idiomatic: When Great Empress Mu's affection faded, on the fifth day of the fifth month Xiaolian was presented to the emperor under the name "Extending Life."

literal: Clever and able to play the pipa, skilled in song and dance.
idiomatic: She was clever, played the pipa well, and excelled at song and dance.

literal: The later lord was infatuated with her: seated they shared one mat; going out they shared one horse — wishing to live and die in one place.
idiomatic: The later lord was infatuated: when seated they shared one mat; when they went out they rode the same horse — he wished never to be parted from her, in life or death.

literal: He ordered the consort to dwell in Longji Hall; the consort hated what Consort Cao had often occupied — he had everything exchanged in place.
idiomatic: He installed her in Longji Hall; she disliked the rooms Consort Cao had favored, and had all their furnishings swapped.

literal: When Zhou troops took Pingyang the emperor was hunting at Sandui; Jinyang urgently reported danger.
idiomatic: When Zhou forces took Pingyang the emperor was hunting at Sandui; urgent dispatches arrived from Jinyang.

literal: The emperor was about to return; the consort requested one more round of the hunt and the emperor followed her word.
idiomatic: The emperor was about to return, but the consort asked for one more circuit of the hunt and he agreed.

literal: Those who understood thought that the later lord's name was Wei — "kill the encirclement" was not an auspicious sign.
idiomatic: Observers noted that the later lord's personal name was Wei — the phrase for "finishing the hunt" also meant "kill the encirclement," an ill omen.

literal: When the emperor reached Jinyang the city was already on the verge of falling.
idiomatic: By the time the emperor reached Jinyang the city was already on the brink of collapse.

literal: They made a tunnel attack; the wall collapsed more than ten paces; soldiers riding the momentum wished to enter.
idiomatic: They attacked by tunnel; the wall gave way for more than ten paces and the soldiers, seizing the moment, meant to rush in.

literal: The emperor ordered a halt for the moment and summoned the consort to watch together.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to wait and summoned the consort to watch with him.

literal: The consort was applying makeup and could not arrive in time.
idiomatic: The consort was still applying her makeup and could not come in time.

literal: The Zhou men blocked it with timbers; the city thus was not taken.
idiomatic: The Zhou stuffed the breach with timbers; the city was not taken.

literal: By old custom it was handed down that on the west of Jinyang city wall there was a sage's footprint on stone; the consort wished to go view it.
idiomatic: Tradition held that on the west side of Jinyang's city wall a sage's footprint was carved in stone; the consort wished to go see it.

literal: The emperor feared crossbow bolts would reach the bridge, so he pulled up the siege timbers to build a long bridge; the supervising builder was punished for not finishing quickly.
idiomatic: Fearing crossbow fire on the bridge, the emperor had siege timbers torn out to build a long bridge; the supervising craftsman was punished for slow work.

literal: The emperor and consort crossed the bridge; the bridge broke; only at night did they return.
idiomatic: The emperor and consort crossed the bridge; it collapsed; they did not return until night.

literal: He said the consort had merit and was about to establish her Left Empress; he immediately sent messengers galloping to fetch feather-embroidered robes and other empress regalia.
idiomatic: He declared the consort had earned merit and was about to make her Left Empress; messengers were sent at once to fetch feather-embroidered robes and other empress regalia.

literal: Still he rode with her together to watch the battle; the eastern flank slightly gave way; the consort in fear said: "The army is defeated!
idiomatic: He still rode with her to watch the battle; when the eastern flank wavered the consort cried in terror, "The army is beaten!

literal: " The emperor then fled back with the consort.
idiomatic: " The emperor at once fled back with her.

literal: At Hongdong garrison the consort was just amusing herself with powder and mirror when behind them came chaotic cries that bandits had come; thereupon they fled again.
idiomatic: At Hongdong garrison the consort was admiring herself in her mirror when confused shouts rose behind them that enemies had come; they fled again.

literal: Inner attendants from Jinyang brought the empress's robes; the emperor steadied the reins and ordered the consort to put them on, then left.
idiomatic: Inner attendants from Jinyang brought the empress's robes; the emperor held the reins and made the consort dress in them before they rode on.

literal: The emperor fled to Ye; the empress dowager arrived later — the emperor did not go out to welcome her;
idiomatic: The emperor fled to Ye; the empress dowager arrived afterward — the emperor did not go out to welcome her;
